newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BALANCED BUDGET SEEN BY YEAR 2000.
newsitem.headline: BALANCED BUDGET SEEN BY YEAR 2000.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Thursday that the country was aiming for a balanced budget by the year 2000.
"The budget deficit now is about two percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and will be balanced by 2000," Shemeta said at a news conference on capital markets and investment in Lithuania.
"We are going to increase revenues by expanding the tax base," Shemeta said.
"In April, revenues were up, and for the first time, our budget is on target," he added.
"We think the earlier practice of not collecting revenue should be terminated," he said.
Tax evasion is regarded as rife in Lithuania.
Lithuania's current right-of-centre government has committed itself to boosting revenues and has declared war on tax evasion.
It also says that it is determined to complete the country's transition to a market economy.
"Our government is a reform government...and we know that reforms are very painful," Shemeta said.
"But the main aim of economic reforms is to accelerate growth," he said.
